paper.title: Non-Asymptotic Pure Exploration by Solving Games

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration (fixed confidence, delta-PAC) for K-armed bandits with exponential family arms
unmapped: general pure exploration query: finite answer set I with correct-answer function i*(mu) over a known structured model set M (covers BAI, Minimum Threshold, structured bandits)
one-parameter exponential family that is sigma^2-sub-Gaussian (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: A pure exploration problem is parameterised by a set $\mathcal M$ of $K$-armed bandit models (the possible environments), a finite set $\mathcal I$ of candidate answers and a correct-answer function $i^* : \mathcal M {\to} \mathcal I$. ... An algorithm is $\delta$-PAC (or $\delta$-correct) if $\pr_\vmu(\ihat \neq i^*(\vmu)) \le \delta$ for each $\vmu \in \mathcal M$.

algorithms.name: Pure exploration meta-algorithm (Algorithm 1: GLRT stopping + optimistic saddle-point learners + tracking)
Any algorithm using GLRT stopping and recommendation rules

conditions: threshold beta(t,delta) satisfies P_mu{GLR_t(mu) > beta(t,delta)} <= delta

source.label: th:GLRT_delta_correct
source.quote: Any algorithm using the GLRT stopping and recommendation rules with threshold $\beta(t,\delta)$ such that $\pr_\vmu\{\mbox{GLR}_t^{\Theta^K}(\{\vmu\}) > \beta(t, \delta)\}\leq \delta$ is $\delta$-correct.

results.notes: delta-correctness of GLRT stopping; essentially a known result (Garivier & Kaufmann 2016) restated.

symbols.T0_delta: max{t in N: t <= beta(t,delta)/D_mu + C_mu(R_t^lambda + R_t^k + h(t))}
symbols.a: concentration parameter a>0 in exploration bonus f
symbols.D_mu: value of the pure exploration game (characteristic complexity 1/T_star)
symbols.C_mu: instance-dependent constant depending on mu and M

conditions: Assumption 2: M contained in [mu_min, mu_max]^K inside Theta
arm distributions in a sigma^2-sub-Gaussian one-parameter exponential family
tuning: R_t^k, R_t^lambda are regret bounds of the two player algorithms

source.label: th:sample_complexity
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{ass:compact_M}, the sample complexity of Algorithm~\ref{alg:the_algorithm} on model $\vmu\in\mathcal{M}$ is \ex_\vmu[\tau_\delta] \leq T_0(\delta) + \frac{2eK}{a^2} with T_0(\delta) = \max \{t\in\N: t \leq \frac{\beta(t,\delta)}{D_\vmu} + C_\vmu(R_t^\vlambda + R_t^k + h(t))\}

results.notes: Implicit bound; asymptotically log(1/delta)/D_mu. Lemma 3 instantiates with AdaHedge vs Best-Response (R_t^k = O(sqrt(t ln K) ln t), R_t^lambda <= 0).

symbols.T0_delta: maximal t in N such that t <= (beta(t,delta)+h(t))/D_mu
symbols.h: 2 sqrt(t) D_mu + 3 L sqrt(2 sigma^2 f(t))(K^2 + (2 sqrt2 + 1/3) sqrt(K t)) + f(t)(K^2 + 2K log(t/K)) + K D
symbols.D_mu: value of the pure exploration game

conditions: Assumption 2 (means in compact interval; L Lipschitz constant and D bound on divergence)

source.quote: Take $b=1$ in the definition of $f(t)$. Let $h(t) = 2\sqrt{t}D_\vmu + 3L\sqrt{2\sigma^2 f(t)}(K^2 + (2\sqrt{2}+\nicefrac{1}{3})\sqrt{Kt}) + f(t)(K^2 + 2K\log(t/K)) + KD$. Then the expected sample complexity is at most $T_0(\delta) + \frac{2eK}{a^2}$, where $T_0(\delta)$ is the maximal $t\in\N$ such that $t \leq (\beta(t,\delta) + h(t))/D_\vmu$ .

results.notes: Requires a max-max-min oracle per step.
